title: Symphonies and string quartets he never got to; nothing fully worked
summary: He always wanted to write five-movement symphonies and quartets; no piece came out as he wanted and the new Atlantic balance is wrong.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Gee, the records sure don't reflect all that care. Going back to composition, most novelists or writers, like, someday maybe I have this vision I'll do a big novel or five or six. Do you have that kind of feeling about compositions you want to do, some long --
I've always wanted to do symphonies. But the last three or four years, I've just lost the energy, man.
(Inaudible) coming back. Got to get my hands back, first.
Yeah. But you meant real, full scale symphonies, three or four movement, that sort of stuff?
Yeah. Have you done string quartets?
Yeah, I thought I remembered something about that. In terms of the compositions you've done so far, are there any that from your point of view really worked the way you wanted them to work?
Always had to make some changes to get the results of what I wanted.
Like this date I just did for Atlantic, the battle of musicians. The balance is not right.
What I've heard. They rush everything, man. It rishes in and out.
